learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the 'magic number' hidden inside every square matrix and use it to solve complex systems of linear equations!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: While a matrix is just a grid of data, a determinant is a single numerical value calculated from a square matrix. It tells you important properties about that matrix, like if it can be inverted.
A Minor is the determinant left over when you cross out a specific row and column. A Cofactor is just the Minor with a '+' or '-' sign attached based on its position.
You can use a 3x3 determinant to instantly calculate the area of a triangle on a graph if you know the coordinates of its three vertices!
You can solve three equations with three variables (x, y, z) simultaneously by finding the inverse of the matrix using determinants and adjoints.

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ The Triangle Trap
fun_activity.instructions: Plot three random points on a piece of graph paper. Form a determinant using their (x, y) coordinates. If the determinant equals zero, your points are trapped on a single straight line (collinear) and don't make a triangle!

exam_tips: 📌 Always expand the determinant along the row or column that has the maximum number of zeros to save time and reduce calculation errors.
📌 Be hyper-aware of your +/- signs when finding cofactors and expanding determinants. One wrong sign ruins the entire 5-mark question.
📌 A matrix is Singular if its determinant is zero ($|A| = 0$). Singular matrices CANNOT be inverted!
quick_recap: ⭐ Determinants can only be calculated for strictly square matrices.
⭐ Adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.
⭐ The Matrix Method is the most reliable way to solve linear equations in board exams.
